cards.explanation: The answer is only murderers, friends. Isaiah says righteousness once resided in her, "…but now only murderers!" (Isaiah 1:21). I think this is a heavy line, and it's okay to let it sit heavy. The city went from full of justice to that.

The answer is water, friends. Isaiah says, "your fine wine is diluted with water." (Isaiah 1:22). Picture me stretching one chocolate chip across an entire batch of cookies. Folks would notice, and I'd be the one blushing at the counter.

The answer is bribes and chasing rewards, friends. Isaiah says, "They all love bribes and chasing after rewards." (Isaiah 1:23). Rulers are supposed to listen to the people in front of them. These rulers were busy listening for the next payoff.

The answer is False, bakers. Isaiah says the rulers "…do not defend the fatherless…" (Isaiah 1:23). God had told His people to defend them (Isaiah 1:17), so this is the opposite of what He asked. The rulers weren't doing what they were supposed to do.

The answer is that He will avenge Himself on them, friends. The Lord GOD of Hosts says, "…avenge Myself on My enemies." (Isaiah 1:24). He says it right alongside being relieved of His foes. It's a serious declaration, and the text lets it stand as it is.
The answer is False, bakers. The Lord says, "I will thoroughly purge your dross; I will remove all your impurities." (Isaiah 1:25). He doesn't say some, He says all. No leftover bits get left behind.

The answer is True, bakers. The Lord says, "I will restore your judges as at first, and your counselors as at the beginning." (Isaiah 1:26). Notice the words as at first and as at the beginning. He points back to how it started.

The answer is False, bakers. The Lord says, "After that you will be called the City of Righteousness, the Faithful City." (Isaiah 1:26). Back in verse 21 Isaiah calls her a harlot, and here she gets a new name instead. The city gets a good name, and that's the last word on it.

The answer is her repentant ones, friends. Isaiah says, "Zion will be redeemed with justice, her repentant ones with righteousness." (Isaiah 1:27). The ones who turn back are the ones named here. It's a short phrase, but it carries a lot.

The answer is False, bakers. Isaiah says, "But rebels and sinners will together be shattered, and those who forsake the LORD will perish." (Isaiah 1:28). The word But marks the turn away from the repentant ones in verse 27. It's a heavy verse, and the text doesn't soften it.

The answer is withered, friends. Isaiah says, "For you will become like an oak whose leaves are withered, like a garden without water." (Isaiah 1:30). Picture a plant that nobody watered, with brown, dried-up leaves. The people delighted in their sacred oaks and gardens, and now they're told what they will become like.

The answer is False, bakers. Isaiah says, "both will burn together, with no one to quench the flames." (Isaiah 1:31). Nobody is there to put it out. I think this is a heavy way to end the passage, so it's good to take it seriously.
